column12: Immersed liquid cooling cabinet
column13: The utility model discloses an immersed liquid cooling cabinet, comprising a cabinet body; the liquid containing box body is arranged in the cabinet body and is used for containing cooling liquid; the at least one server mounting position is arranged in the liquid containing box body; the at least one switch mounting position is vertically arranged at the periphery of the liquid containing box body; and the wire passing device assemblies are fixedly installed at the tops of the switch installation positions, and cables of the switches installed at the corresponding switch installation positions are arranged in the wire passing device assemblies in a penetrating mode. According to the immersed liquid-cooled cabinet structure, layout, installation and wiring of the switch are fully considered, and the rationality of the overall structure is improved; and a fusion installation technology of the switch and the server is adopted, so that the immersed liquid-cooled cabinet has more compact space utilization and more tidy and beautiful appearance.

column12: SINGLE-PHASE IMMERSION LIQUID-COOLING CABINET
column13: The present application discloses an immersion liquid-cooling cabinet comprising: a cabinet body; a liquid containing tank body mounted in the cabinet body for containing a cooling liquid; at least one server mounting position provided within the liquid containing tank body; at least one switch mounting position vertically provided around the liquid containing tank body; a cable-passing device assembly fixedly mounted on top of the switch mounting position, within which a cable of a switch mounted at the corresponding switch mounting position is routed. The structure of the immersion liquid-cooling cabinet gives full consideration to the layout, installation and wiring of the switch, thereby improving the rationality of the overall structure; and an integrated installation technology for the switch and the server is adopted, so that the immersion liquid-cooling cabinet is more compact in space utilization and more neat and beautiful in appearance.

column12: SINGLE-PHASE IMMERSION LIQUID-COOLED CABINET
column13: Disclosed in the present disclosure is an immersion liquid-cooled cabinet, comprising: a cabinet body; a liquid containing tank, which is mounted in the cabinet body and is configured to contain a coolant; at least one server mounting position, which is arranged in the liquid containing tank; at least one switch mounting position, which is vertically arranged on the periphery of the liquid containing tank; and a wire-passing device assembly, which is fixedly mounted at the top of the switch mounting position, wherein a cable of a switch mounted on the corresponding switch mounting position penetrates the wire-passing device assembly. The structure of the immersion liquid-cooled cabinet fully takes into account the layout, mounting and wiring of the switch, thereby improving the rationality of the overall structure; and by using an integrated mounting technique for the switch and the server, the immersion liquid-cooled cabinet has a more compact utilization space and a tidier and more attractive appearance. column12: Liquid submerged, horizontal computer server rack and systems and method of cooling such a server rack
column13: An apparatus for cooling a plurality of rack-mountable servers containing heat generating electronic components in a server room including a dielectric liquid cooling apparatus located inside the tank and a secondary cooling apparatus comprising a remote heat exchanger and at least one pump. The volume of dielectric liquid coolant comprises at least one passage in the tank that is outside of the vertically oriented rack-mountable servers. When the at least one pump is operated to move the dielectric liquid coolant vertically across the heat producing components on the vertically oriented servers, a circuit is formed in which a first portion of dielectric liquid coolant is moved vertically upward across the heat producing components on the vertically oriented servers and then downward outside of the rack mountable servers in the at least one passage, while a second portion of the dielectric liquid coolant flows out of the tank.

column12: Liquid cooling cabinet, liquid cooling equipment and liquid cooling system
column13: The utility model provides a liquid cooling cabinet, a liquid cooling device and a liquid cooling system, the liquid cooling cabinet comprises a cabinet body, a liquid inlet pipe, a liquid outlet pipe and at least one first guide pipe, and a cavity used for loading a server and bearing cooling liquid is formed in the cabinet body; a liquid outlet is formed in the pipe wall of the liquid inlet pipe, and the liquid inlet pipe is used for supplementing cooling liquid for the cavity through the liquid outlet; one end of the first guide pipe is correspondingly connected with the liquid outlet, and the other end of the first guide pipe is used for spraying cooling liquid; the liquid outlet pipe is located in the cavity and used for discharging the cooling liquid. Through the first guide pipe, the cooling liquid is finely sprayed to the determined position in the cavity of the liquid cooling cabinet, meanwhile, the fluid disturbance effect of the cooling liquid in the cavity is enhanced, and the heat exchange efficiency is improved.

column12: Liquid-cooled server heat dissipation system and heat dissipation control method and device
column13: The invention discloses a liquid-cooled server heat dissipation system and a heat dissipation control method and device to improve the heat dissipation efficiency of the liquid-cooled server heat dissipation system and save system energy consumption, thereby reducing the PUE of a data center. The liquid-cooled server heat dissipation system comprises a liquid cooling system and an air cooling system. The liquid cooling system comprises the hot side of a surface-type heat exchanger and a plurality of liquid-cooled servers located in an equipment cabinet which are located in a first circulationloop and connected in series. The air cooling system includes an evaporator, an evaporator fan and the cold side of the surface-type heat exchanger. The evaporator and the cold side of the surface-type heat exchanger are located in a second circulation loop and are successively connected. The evaporator fan is disposed opposite to the evaporator.

column12: Sealing leak detection device and immersed liquid cooling air conditioner

The adjustable pressing plate is arranged to cover the upper surface of the inflatable sealing ring when sliding towards the outer side. The immersed liquid-cooled air conditioner comprises the sealed leak detection device and a liquid-cooled air conditioner system, and the sealed leak detection device is installed above the liquid-cooled air conditioner system. The sealing leak detection device not only can realize leak detection of the liquid container, but also can solve the leak detection problem of a whole machine system. The sealing leak detection device has the characteristics of simple equipment, strong operability, low cost, high efficiency and the like, and does not pollute the whole liquid cooling air conditioning system. The sealing leak detection device provides a brand-new technical method for solving the sealing leak detection of the complete machine system of the immersed liquid-cooled air conditioner.

column12: Negative pressure liquid cooling system and control method and control device thereof
column13: The invention provides a negative pressure liquid cooling system and a control method and device thereof. The system comprises a vacuum pump, a liquid storage cavity, a negative pressure energy storage cavity, a liquid cooling server, a bubble detection device, a liquid pump, a plate heat exchanger, a first adjusting valve, a second adjusting valve, a third adjusting valve, a fourth adjusting valve, a fifth adjusting valve, a first one-way valve and a controller. Under the condition that the air content in the negative pressure liquid cooling system is determined to be greater than a threshold value through the bubble detection device, the controller controls the liquid cooling server to be closed, controls the vacuum pump, the third regulating valve, the fourth regulating valve and the fifth regulating valve to be opened, and controls the first regulating valve and the second regulating valve to be closed; and the liquid in the liquid cooling server flows into the liquid storage cavity and the negative pressure energy storage cavity. Due to the fact that the liquid storage cavity and the negative pressure energy storage cavity are both in the negative pressure state, when leakage points happen to a cold plate pipeline in the liquid cooling server, liquid can flow into the liquid storage cavity and the negative pressure energy storage cavity, and the risk that cooling liquid leaks into the server can be reduced.

The cabinet comprises a cabinet body, a first liquid inlet pipe and a liquid outlet pipe, wherein a cavity for loading a server and accommodating cooling liquid is formed in the cabinet body; the first liquid inlet pipe is used for injecting cooling liquid, and at least one first liquid inlet is formed in the first liquid inlet pipe; the first liquid inlet is used for being connected with a liquid guide pipe of the server, and the liquid guide pipe of the server is connected with a heating component of the server so as to dissipate heat of the heating component; the first liquid inlet is provided with an opening and closing assembly, and the opening and closing assembly is configured to be used for closing or opening the first liquid inlet; the liquid outlet pipe is located in the cavity, communicates with the interior of the cavity and is used for discharging the cooling liquid in the cavity. The cabinet is used for improving the cooling capacity of a system and improving the heat dissipation efficiency.

column12: COOLANT SHROUD

The side walls mounted on a mounting surface within the immersion coolant tank and on which the heatsink is secured and at least one of the side walls includes a fluid port and a fluid aperture. Dielectric fluid inside the cooling chamber is in fluid communication with dielectric fluid outside the cooling chamber via the fluid aperture. The fluid port is in fluid communication with a dielectric fluid pump disposed outside the cooling chamber.

column12: LIQUID COOLING CABINET, APPARATUS AND SYSTEM
column13: The present disclosure provides a liquid cooling cabinet, apparatus and system. The liquid cooling cabinet comprises a cabinet body, a liquid inlet pipe, a liquid outlet pipe, and at least one first guide pipe; a chamber configured to load a server and bear a cooling liquid is formed in the cabinet body; a liquid outlet is formed in the wall of the liquid inlet pipe, and the liquid inlet pipe is configured to supplement the cooling liquid for the chamber through the liquid outlet; one end of the first guide pipe is correspondingly connected to the liquid outlet, and the other end of the first guide pipe is configured to spray the cooling liquid; and the liquid outlet pipe is located inside the chamber and configured to discharge the cooling liquid. The cooling liquid is accurately sprayed to a determined position in the chamber of the liquid cooling cabinet by means of the first guide pipe, and additionally, the fluid disturbance effect of the cooling liquid in the chamber is enhanced, thereby improving the heat exchange efficiency.

column12: Spraying type liquid cooling method and device, electronic equipment and storage medium
column13: The invention provides a spraying type liquid cooling method and device, electronic equipment and a storage medium, the spraying type liquid cooling device comprises a box body, and the box body is internally provided with at least one main liquid pipe, a plurality of branch liquid pipes, a liquid outlet pipe, a server installation position and a cooling liquid recovery tank; the main liquid pipe is connected with the plurality of branch liquid pipes; at least one row of liquid separation holes are formed in the liquid separation pipe; the cooling liquid recovery tank is connected with the liquid outlet pipe; the server mounting position is used for vertically or obliquely placing a server; cooling liquid in the main liquid pipe flows to the liquid distribution pipes and is sprayed to the server through liquid distribution holes in the liquid distribution pipes so as to take away heat of the server; the cooling liquid recovery tank is used for collecting the cooling liquid sprayed by the liquid separation holes; the liquid outlet pipe is used for discharging the cooling liquid from the box body, the upper portion or the side face of the server which is vertically or obliquely placed can share the main liquid pipe and the branch liquid pipe of the same height space area, and space saving is facilitated.

column12: Liquid cooling radiator
column13: The utility model provides a liquid cooling radiator comprising a main body structure, the main body structure is provided with a heat exchange surface, the heat exchange surface is used for exchanging heat with a power unit, and a plurality of main flow channels arranged in parallel are distributed along the heat exchange surface in the main body structure; wherein each main flow channel is internally provided with a reinforced heat dissipation section, each reinforced heat dissipation section is internally provided with a plurality of small flow channels which are connected in parallel, and the reinforced heat dissipation sections correspond to the power units in position. In the scheme, the plurality of small flow channels which are connected in parallel are arranged in the reinforced heat dissipation section, corresponding to the mounting position of the power unit, in the main flow channel, so that on one hand, the contact area between the side walls of the plurality of small flow channels and cooling fluid is increased, heat dissipation of heat generated by the power unit is accelerated, on the other hand, the speed of the fluid in the small flow channels is accelerated, and the heat dissipation efficiency is improved. And the turbulent flow effect of the fluid is also improved, so that heat in a heat concentration area can be quickly taken out, and the heat exchange efficiency of the whole liquid cooling radiator is improved.

column12: Liquid cooling cabinet, equipment and system

The cabinet comprises a cabinet body, a first liquid inlet pipe and a liquid outlet pipe, wherein a cavity for loading a server and accommodating cooling liquid is formed in the cabinet body; the first liquid inlet pipe is used for injecting cooling liquid, and at least one first liquid inlet is formed in the first liquid inlet pipe; the first liquid inlet is used for being connected with a liquid guide pipe of a server, the liquid guide pipe of the server is communicated with the interior of the server, and cooling liquid flows into the server through the liquid guide pipe and flows out of the server to the cavity; the first liquid inlet is provided with an opening and closing assembly, and the opening and closing assembly is configured to be that when the liquid guide pipe is inserted into the first liquid inlet, the first liquid inlet is opened; when the liquid guide pipe is pulled out of the first liquid inlet, the first liquid inlet is closed; the liquid outlet pipe is located in the cavity, communicates with the interior of the cavity and is used for discharging the cooling liquid in the cavity. The cabinet is used for improving the cooling capacity of a system and improving the heat dissipation efficiency.

column12: Liquid cooling system
column13: The utility model provides a liquid cooling system. The system comprises a heat exchange module and an equipment module. Wherein the primary side input end of the heat exchange module is connected with the water taking device, and the primary side output end of the heat exchange module is connected with the drainage device; the secondary side output end of the heat exchange module is connected with the first water outlet end of the equipment module, the first water outlet end of the equipment module is connected with the water inlet end of the air conditioner, the first water inlet end of the equipment module is connected with the water outlet end of the air conditioner, and the first water inlet end of the equipment module is connected with the second water outlet end of the equipment module. The second water outlet end of the equipment module is connected with the water inlet end of the server unit, the second water inlet end of the equipment module is connected with the water outlet end of the server unit, and the second water inlet end of the equipment module is connected with the secondary side input end of the heat exchange module; and the heat exchange module is used for cooling the cooling liquid of the air conditioner and/or the server unit by using the underground water pumped by the water taking device. The system is used for reducing refrigeration water consumption.

column12: Liquid cooling cabinet
column13: The utility model provides a liquid cooling cabinet, which comprises a cabinet body provided with a cooling cavity used for containing cooling liquid; the circulating pipeline comprises an inner pipeline and an outer pipeline which are communicated with each other, the inner pipeline is arranged in the cooling cavity, a circulating hole is formed in the inner pipeline, the circulating hole is communicated with the cooling cavity so that cooling liquid can circulate, and the outer pipeline is used for being connected with heat exchange equipment; the connecting structure is arranged on the cabinet body and provided with a first end and a second end which are oppositely arranged, the first end is located in the cooling cavity, the second end is located outside the cooling cavity, the connecting structure is provided with a communicating channel, the two ends of the communicating channel extend to the end faces of the first end and the second end respectively, and the first end is detachably connected with the inner pipeline; the second end is detachably connected with the outer pipeline, so that the inner pipeline and the outer pipeline are communicated with each other through a connecting structure. Through the technical scheme provided by the invention, the problem that the processing difficulty is high when the circulating pipeline and the cabinet body are connected in a welding manner in the prior art can be solved.

column12: SERVER BASKET FOR USE IN AN IMMERSION COOLING TANK
column13: Server baskets for use in immersion tanks are described herein. In one example, a server basket may be configured to receive a computer server. The server basket may include a cable management housing that has one or more data and power ports. The cable management housing may be located at or proximate to a top portion of the server basket. When the server basket is immersed in dielectric fluid in an immersion tank, the cable management housing may be located above a liquid level, thereby providing convenient access to the one or more ports. A signal repeater may be located in the cable management housing and above the liquid level. The server basket may include support arms that can be deployed when removing the server from the dielectric fluid. The support arms may enable drip drying and fluid recapture by the immersion tank. Other examples may be claimed or described.

column12: HYBRID COOLING SYSTEMS TO COOL MULTI-CHIP MODULES
column13: A hybrid cooler has a first condenser block and a second condenser block. The liquid-cooled cold plate is positioned between the first passive cold plate and the second passive cold plate.

column12: Coolant Flow Enhancement
column13: An immersion cooling system including an immersion coolant tank, a heat exchanger, and an eductor. The immersion coolant tank contains the heat generating electronic equipment. The heat exchanger removes heat absorbed by a first portion of a volume of dielectric cooling fluid within the immersion coolant tank. The eductor receives the first portion of the volume of dielectric cooling fluid through a first port from the heat exchanger as motive fluid and receives a second portion of the volume of dielectric cooling fluid from the immersion coolant tank through a second port as a suction fluid. The motive fluid may create suction by passing through the eductor, which suction draws the suction fluid into the eductor. The eductor may also mix the motive fluid with the suction fluid inside the eductor; and releasing the mixture of the motive fluid and the suction fluid through a third port.

column12: Method and apparatus for recovering dielectric fluids used for immersion cooling
column13: A method of and system for recovering a dielectric fluid used for immersion cooling of electronic devices, the method including filtering the dielectric fluid to remove a first group of solid contaminants; distilling the filtered dielectric fluid in one or more distillation tanks to produce a vaporized dielectric fluid; separating the vaporized dielectric fluid from less volatile contaminants, such that the vaporized dielectric fluid is introduced as a condensate into a circulation tank; circulating the condensate by pumping the condensate from the circulation tank through one or more filters; filtering the circulating condensate through the filter(s) to remove a second group of contaminants; and returning the filtered condensate to the circulation tank.

The baffle assembly may be removably attachable to the electronic device. In one embodiment, the baffle assembly may include a plate having one or more slots. The baffle assembly may include one or more posts extending from the plate and being configured to attach to a substrate of the electronic device. The baffle assembly may include a baffle that is removably attachable to the one or more slots. Other examples may be claimed or described.

As but one example, some disclosed liquid-cooled heat exchangers incorporate a leak-detection sensor, which, in turn, can couple with a computing environment that monitors for detected leaks, and, responsive to an indication of a detected leak, invokes a task to control or to mitigate the detected leak.

column12: Method and system for in-situ measuring of a heat transfer fluid in a device for immersion cooling and device for immersion cooling
column13: A method and system for controlling operation of an immersion cooling system having an immersion cooling tank adapted to contain a heat transfer fluid used to immersion cool a heat-generating object contained therein, the method including: sampling a volume of the heat transfer fluid while the object remains in an operating state; measuring at least one property or parameter of the sampled heat transfer fluid; generating and transmitting measurement data to a control unit; comparing measurement data with respective threshold data using the control unit; and controlling operation of the immersion cooling system with the control unit based on the comparison.

column13: In some respects, concepts disclosed herein generally concern systems, methods and components to detect a presence of a liquid externally of a desired primary flow path through a segment of a fluid circuit, e.g., throughout a cooling loop. As but one example, some disclosed liquid-cooled heat exchangers incorporate a leak-detection sensor, which, in turn, can couple with a computing environment that monitors for detected leaks, and, responsive to an indication of a detected leak, invokes a task to control or to mitigate the detected leak.

column12: IMMERSION COOLING RESERVOIR LEVEL CONTROL
column13: Various embodiments include first and second coolant level regulator components of first and second component cooling tanks and a processor. Each of the first and second coolant level regulator components may include a temperature sensor configured to measure a temperature of the coolant in a reservoir, a coolant release valve configured to regulate the release of coolant from the reservoir, and a coolant level detector configured to detect a level of the coolant in the reservoir. The processor may receive temperature measurements from the temperature sensors, signal a target coolant level update for adjusting a level of the coolant in the reservoir by the coolant release valve. The target coolant level update may be determined based on a temperature average of the received temperature measurements from the temperature sensors. The coolant release valve may adjust a release of the coolant from the reservoir based on the target coolant level update.

column12: Immersed cooled reservoir level control
column13: Various embodiments of the present application include first and second coolant level regulator components of a first and second component cooling tank and a processor. The first and second coolant level regulator components may each include: a temperature sensor configured to measure a coolant temperature in the reservoir; a coolant release valve configured to regulate release of the coolant from the reservoir; and a coolant level detector configured to detect a level of the coolant in the reservoir. The processor may receive a temperature measurement from the temperature sensor and send a signal of a target coolant level update for adjusting the coolant level in the reservoir through the coolant relief valve. The target coolant level update may be determined based on a temperature average of the temperature measurements received from the temperature sensor. The coolant release valve may regulate release of coolant from the reservoir based on the target coolant level update.

column12: Cooling system and control method thereof
column13: The invention provides a cooling system and a control method thereof, and relates to the technical field of data centers. The cooling system comprises an air cooling module, a liquid cooling module, a heat dissipation module and a first heat exchanger. The first heat exchanger comprises a first heat exchange flow channel and a second heat exchange flow channel. The heat dissipation module comprises a first inlet end and a first outlet end, the air cooling module comprises a second inlet end and a second outlet end, the first heat exchange flow channel comprises a third inlet end and a third outlet end, the second heat exchange flow channel comprises a fourth inlet end and a fourth outlet end, and the liquid cooling module comprises a fifth inlet end and a fifth outlet end. The first outlet end is used for communicating with the second inlet end, the second outlet end is used for communicating with the third inlet end, and the third outlet end is used for communicating with the first inlet end. The fifth outlet end is used for being communicated with the fourth inlet end, and the fourth outlet end is used for being communicated with the fifth inlet end. The cooling system provided by the invention is relatively simple in structure and relatively high in energy efficiency.

column12: APPARATUS AND METHOD FOR CONTROLLING COOLANT FLOW OF IMMERSION COOLING TYPE

column12: DEVICE FOR PROVIDING IMMERSIVE CONTENT AND METHOD FOR PROVIDING IMMERSIVE CONTENT
column13: Disclosed are a device for providing immersive content and a method thereof. The device for providing immersive content disclosed herein may comprise: a communication module configured to communicate with a cloud server and receive sensing data from one or more sensors disposed around a swimming pool; and memory for storing immersive content and 3D data related to same. In addition, the device can: recognize, on the basis of the sensing data received through the one or more sensors, the situation of a mobile object that has entered the vicinity of the swimming pool; and select immersive content related to the recognized situation of the mobile object and render the selected immersive content so as to output same as augmented reality on an underwater surface of the swimming pool. Here, the rendered immersive content is adaptively varied in response to changes in the situation of the mobile object.

column12: Fluid heat exchange systems
column13: A fluid heat exchanger includes: a heat spreader plate including an intended heat generating component contact region; a plurality of microchannels for directing heat transfer fluid over the heat spreader plate, the plurality of microchannels each having a first end and an opposite end and each of the plurality of microchannels extending substantially parallel with each other microchannel and each of the plurality of microchannels having a continuous channel flow path between their first end and their opposite end; a fluid inlet opening for the plurality of microchannels and positioned between the microchannel first and opposite ends, a first fluid outlet opening from the plurality of microchannels at each of the microchannel first ends; and an opposite fluid outlet opening from the plurality of microchannels at each of the microchannel opposite ends, the fluid inlet opening and the first and opposite fluid outlet openings providing that any flow of heat transfer fluid that passes into the plurality of microchannels, flows along the full length of each of the plurality of microchannels in two directions outwardly from the fluid inlet opening. A method of cooling a heat generating component uses a fluid heat exchanger that splits a mass flow of coolant.

column12: TELECOMMUNICATIONS EQUIPMENT ENCLOSURES HAVING HEAT EXCHANGERS
column13: A telecommunications equipment enclosure includes a plurality of walls defining a chamber for housing a heat generating component, an air heat exchanger, and at least two fans. The air heat exchanger defines a first airflow path through the air heat exchanger and internal to the chamber, and a second airflow path through the air heat exchanger and external to the chamber. The at least two fans are positioned in a series airflow arrangement in the first airflow path or the second airflow path. The at least two fans are configured to move air through the first airflow path or the second airflow path to remove heat from the chamber. Other examples telecommunications equipment enclosures are also disclose.

column12: TWO-PHASE IMMERSION COOLING SYSTEM
column13: A two-phase immersion cooling system can include a pressure vessel with one or more processors, a two-phase refrigerant, and one or more condenser tubes within the vessel. The refrigerant can flow past the processor(s) by thermosyphon. The refrigerant can be configured to extract heat from the processor(s). In at least one embodiment, a liquid phase of the refrigerant can fully, or at least partially, cover the processor(s). The condenser tube(s) can be configured to receive cooling fluid into and transmit cooling fluid out of the vessel, thereby removing heat from the vessel.

A method of cooling a heat generating component uses a fluid heat exchanger that splits a mass flow of coolant.

column12: IMMERSION COOLING TYPE APPARATUS AND METHOD FOR CONTROLLING FLOW
column13: The present invention relates to an immersion cooling type apparatus and method for controlling a flow, the apparatus including a pump connected to a tank, in which a target to be cooled is installed and a coolant is accommodated, and configured to circulate the coolant accommodated in the tank, a first temperature sensor installed in the tank and configured to measure a temperature of the coolant, a second temperature sensor installed at the target to be cooled and configured to measure a temperature of the target to be cooled, and a processor configured to determine whether a change in the temperature of the target to be cooled is normal based on data of the target to be cooled, and in a case where the change is normal, determine whether an operation of the pump is necessary based on the temperature of the target to be cooled and the temperature of the coolant, and control a flow of the coolant using the pump. column12: Fluid heat exchanger
column13: A fluid heat exchanger for cooling an electronic device can have a plurality of walls. The walls can define a corresponding plurality of microchannels. Each microchannel can extend from a first end to a second end. The plurality of microchannels can define at least two opposed outer microchannels and a centrally located microchannel positioned between the opposed outer microchannels. A fluid inlet passage can be configured to deliver a heat-exchange fluid to each microchannel between the corresponding first end and the corresponding second end of the respective microchannel. A fluid outlet passage can have an enlarged outlet region from the centrally located microchannel compared to a corresponding outlet region from one or both of the opposed outer microchannels. Related methods are disclosed.

column12: LIQUID LEVEL SENSING MODULE, NON-TRANSITORY COMPUTER READABLE MEDIUM, AND DEVICE HOUSING
column13: The invention provides a liquid level sensing module, a non-transitory computer readable medium and a device housing. The liquid level sensing module is provided with a device housing for accommodating an electronic device. The liquid level sensing module includes a liquid level sensor and a controller coupled to the liquid level sensor and configured to: receive a signal from the liquid level sensor and indicative of a height of a dielectric liquid in the device housing; receive a signal from a pump controller indicative of a volume of dielectric fluid provided to the device housing; and generating a dielectric fluid volume map in the device housing based on the signal from the liquid level sensor and the signal from the pump controller. column12: HEAT EXCHANGER WITH CONTACT SEALING AND RELATED SYSTEMS
column13: A heat exchanger conveys heat from a heat-generating component to a coolant. The heat exchanger includes a heat spreader plate defining an upper surface. A plurality of fins extend transversely from the upper surface to respective distal fin edges. The plurality of fins define a corresponding plurality of microchannels. A housing defines an underside surface positioned overtop the distal fin edges. The underside surface urges against the distal fin edges sufficiently to substantially inhibit a coolant from leaking from one microchannel to an adjacent microchannel. The fins can be sufficiently compressed between the heat spreader plate and the underside of the housing as to deflect the fins from an unloaded, at-rest orientation. The distal edges of the fins can be flared laterally outward. Such flared distal fin edges can be fused with the underside of the housing and the microchannels can be substantially free of any fusing material.

column12: Heat exchange amount testing system and equipment
column13: The utility model discloses a heat exchange amount testing system and equipment, which are used for testing the heat exchange amount of the secondary side of a CDU. The heat exchange amount testing system comprises a closed box body, measuring equipment and temperature adjusting equipment arranged in the closed box body, liquid is contained in the closed box body, the closed box body comprises a liquid supply interface and a liquid return interface, the liquid supply interface is connected with tested equipment through a first pipeline, the liquid return interface is connected with the tested equipment through a second pipeline, and the temperature adjusting equipment is arranged in the closed box body. When a heat exchange amount test is carried out on the tested equipment, liquid in the closed box body flows to the tested equipment through the first pipeline and flows back to the closed box body through the second pipeline; the temperature adjusting equipment is used for adjusting the temperature of the liquid in the closed box body in the heat exchange amount testing process and keeping the temperature of the liquid constant; and the measuring equipment is used for determining the heat exchange amount of the measured equipment.

column12: FLUID HEAT EXCHANGER CONFIGURED TO PROVIDE A SPLIT FLOW
column13: A fluid heat exchanger for cooling an electronic device can have a plurality of walls. The walls can define a corresponding plurality of microchannels. Each microchannel can extend from a first end to a second end. The plurality of microchannels can define at least two opposed outer microchannels and a centrally located microchannel positioned between the opposed outer microchannels. A fluid inlet passage can be configured to deliver a heat-exchange fluid to each microchannel between the corresponding first end and the corresponding second end of the respective microchannel. A fluid outlet passage can have an enlarged outlet region from the centrally located microchannel compared to a corresponding outlet region from one or both of the opposed outer microchannels. Related methods are disclosed.

column12: COUPON AUTOMATIC CLEANING EQUIPMENT
column13: [0098] Coupon cleaning for testing and analysis can be automated to reduce potential exposure to liquid solutions and to more quickly and efficiently clean multiple coupons. A robotic arm (18) is controlled and programmed to connect to one or more coupons (46) and to move the coupons (46) along a guide. The arm (18) then submerges the coupon (46) into multiple solutions and/or water in a predetermined sequence to clean the coupon. The coupon (46) is then replaced on a rack (26) to dry before being measured and analyzed. The process is automated in that no human is needed to contact the coupons or to move them through the cleaning sequence, which provides a safer process for cleaning of the coupons.

column12: TOTAL HEAT EXCHANGER
column13: The present invention relates to a total heat exchanger easy to switch between a total heat exchange mode and a bypass mode. According to one embodiment of the present invention, the total heat exchanger comprises a housing, a heat exchange unit, an upper air guide, and a louver device. The housing has a ventilation hole and an air inlet formed on one side surface, and has an outer air hole and an air outlet formed on the other side surface, which is an opposite side to the one side surface. The heat exchange unit is received inside the housing and includes a total heat exchange element to exchange heat between air sucked through the outer air hole and the air sucked through the ventilation hole. The upper air guide forms a bypass flow path allowing the ventilation hole to communicate with the air outlet on an upper side of the heat exchange unit. The louver device is installed between the ventilation hole and the heat exchange unit, and allows the ventilation hole to communicate with the total heat exchange element or the bypass flow path. The louver device includes: a driving motor; a pinion connected to the driving motor; a driving link including a rack part engaged with the pinion; a rotary shaft link connected to the driving link to be able to rotate; and a rotary shaft connected to the rotary shaft link, and simultaneously rotating a bypass louver corresponding to the bypass flow path and a heat exchange louver corresponding to the total heat exchange element.

column12: HEAT EXCHANGER

column13: The present invention relates to a heat exchanger. The heat exchanger according to the present invention comprises: a pin which is provided with a corrugated portion formed with a ridge having an edged upper end and a valley having an edged lower end; a tube insertion port which is formed by opening a part of the corrugated portion; and a pin collar which is formed to vertically protrude from the circumference of the tube's corrugated portion. The upper end of the ridges are rounded to have a round value (R1) 1.25 times of the height (h1) of the ridge. In addition, the lower end of the valley is rounded to have a round value (R2) 1.5 times of the depth (h2) of the valley. The upper end of the ridge and/or the lower end of the valley are processed to be rounded significantly so that fluids flowing between the pins can smoothly flow even on the upper end of the ridge or the lower end of the valley where an inclination is rapidly changed without being congested, thereby reducing pressure loss of the fluids and improving heat exchanger performance.

column12: METHODS AND SYSTEMS OF STREAMING REFRIGERANT IN A HEAT EXCHANGER
column13: Embodiments are disclosed to help create longitudinal refrigerant streams, for example, in a shell and tube type evaporator, so as to manage refrigerant and/or lubricant in the evaporator. In some embodiments, the shell side of the evaporator may include a plurality of longitudinally extended pans stacked in a vertical direction. In some embodiments, refrigerant can be directed onto a top pan. The refrigerant can form a longitudinal refrigerant stream along the pan and flow down to the next pan in the vertical direction and form another longitudinal refrigerant stream. column12: METHOD FOR FORMING LUBRICATING LAYER OF HEAT EXCHANGER
column13: The present invention relates to a method for forming a lubricating layer of a heat exchanger, capable of maintaining durability for a long term. The method for forming the lubricating layer of the heat exchanger provided in the present invention includes: a pre-processing step of forming pores in a surface formed of aluminum constituting a refrigerant pipe or a cooling fin of the heat exchanger or improving the roughness of the surface including the aluminum; a binder layer forming step of putting the aluminum into a polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) aqueous solution, drawing the aluminum from the aqueous solution, and drying the aluminum; and (c) a lubricating layer forming step of putting the aluminum into fluorinated oil, drawing the aluminum from the fluorine-based oil, and drying the aluminum. The drying in the lubricating layer forming step (c) includes: (c1) placing the aluminum drawn from the fluorinated oil on an inclined surface and leaving the aluminum in a tilted state; (c2) a step of primarily drying the aluminum for a specific time at a specific temperature; and (c3) a step of secondarily drying the aluminum at a temperature lower than the drying temperature of the primary drying step and for a time longer than the drying time in the primary drying step.
